newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat to up 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat to up 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were assessed from unchanged to about one-eighth of a point higher, mainly bolstered by firmer Treasuries, as activity remained light in post-Christmas trade.
What few trades there were appeared to be concentrated in the short-end of the municipal market, though traders said that there were several bid-wanted lists circulated.

Would-be sellers seemed to be trying to get rid of shorter-term paper with undesirable call features. "I think they're trying to move out further in the curve, around 15-20 years," one said, adding this positioning reflected underlying bullish sentiment.
There was speculation that the amount of municipal bonds redeemed in January might be below last year's level, as 1996 was 10 years after the Tax Reform Act was approved.
This could reduce the amount of money that typically flows into the municipal market in January, when investors roll cash from bonds that have been redeemed into new issues.

The market was looking ahead to the release on Friday of jobless claims, which were predicted at 346,000 in the week ended December 21, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists, while durable goods for November were forecast at 0.1 percent higher.
However, with many brokerage houses operating with short staffs due to the Christmas holidays, the market's reaction might be subdued unless the data contain surprises.

Actively quoted issues in the municipal market included Florida Ports Financing Community Revenues of June 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.73 percent NET, down one basis point.

The March U.S. Treasury futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade fell two ticks to 113-11/32, while the March municipal bond futures rose four ticks to 116-9/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts stood at plus 94 ticks.
